old_phrase: (round-2 README/script) '好辨识参数 max|z| -- Nc 0.039, Nv 0.038, mu_n 0.027, mu_p 0.035, tau_HTL 0.022 -> 全部 <= 0.04 sigma, 不敏感'
corrected: That number was the RAW normalized |d_mu| (<=0.04 in 0..1 normalized-log10 units) read from the buggy stored z=d column and printed as if it were sigma units. With z_ref = d_mu/sigma_ref (m=1 reference sigma), the FINE chain (m0.35/m0.25 @1e-6 vs ref, 6 reps) moves the point estimate of EVERY parameter by 0.3-0.7 sigma_ref (mu_p 0.57, mu_n 0.47, Nv 0.43, tau_HTL 0.44, Nc 0.32, rad_c 0.71, tau_ETL 0.38; see e2v3_fine_chain_perparam.csv). In log10-decade units the movement is 0.10-0.48 decade. The round-2 claim 'well-identified params are mesh-insensitive' does NOT survive; sigma is the model's own predictive width and z is therefore a within-model ruler, not a statement about global identifiability.

old_phrase: (README §5.2) 敏感只发生于弱辨识参数；好辨识参数不敏感
corrected: Once sigma-normalised (z_ref = d_mu/sigma_ref) the FINE chain moves well-identified params too (mu_p 0.57, mu_n 0.47, Nc 0.32 sigma_ref), so 'only weak parameters are sensitive' is false as stated. What is true: (a) the largest sigma-normalised and log10-decade shifts are on wide-sigma params (rad_c 0.71 sigma_ref / 0.48 decade), and (b) the window-substitution attribution shows the movement follows whichever parent supplies the >1 V (mesh-unconverged) tail. 'Weak parameter' is a relative label (wide predictive sigma), not an intrinsic cause.

old_phrase: (README §3) rad_c/tau_ETL 的 sigma 常触顶 1.0 (= 整个先验宽 3 decade)
corrected: False for the 66 curves: no sigma hits the 1.0 clip top (nor the 0.01 floor). sigma_norm range 0.02-0.40 (tau_ETL max ~0.40); physical-log10 sigma = sigma_norm*R[j], up to ~1.6 log10-decade for tau_ETL (R=4), ~0.5-0.9 for rad_c (R=3). The 0.1-sigma criterion is NOT diluted by clipping for this data set.

old_phrase: (README §4) 窗互换证明该弱参数敏感性完全由 >1 V 尾巴驱动 / 证明非代码错误
corrected: Window substitution is an ATTRIBUTION diagnostic: swapping which parent supplies the >1 V segment flips mu toward that parent. It supports the 'inverse reads the >1 V tail' mechanism but is not an independent reverse model, does not establish which segment is 'correct', and cannot by itself rule out other encoder/geometry artefacts.

old_phrase: (README §0/§5) 发电窗内反演稳健 / mesh floor << inverse uncertainty (global)
corrected: Only the CURVES in the <=1 V / gen0 window are mesh-converged. The frozen VAE reads the FULL 0-1.3 V curve; replacing the >1 V segment moves weak-parameter point estimates by up to ~0.16 sigma_ref. A global claim 'mesh floor << inverse uncertainty' therefore only holds for narrow-sigma parameters and must be stated with the >1 V caveat.
